title: ₹36 Crore and Counting: 'Welcome To The Jungle' Is the Big, Loud, Glorious Stress-Buster Bollywood Needed
excerpt: Akshay Kumar and 33 of his closest friends just delivered the third-biggest opening of 2026 — and Saturday's numbers are climbing by the hour
body:
Somewhere around the three-minute mark of *Welcome To The Jungle*, **Akshay Kumar** walks into a room wearing an expression that says he knows exactly how ridiculous this movie is going to be — and he's delighted about it. That energy, apparently, is contagious.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=R704yP3dlXw</youtube>

The third instalment of the *Welcome* franchise hit theatres on Friday after Thursday paid previews, and the numbers are already telling a story the industry desperately wanted to hear: **families are back in cinemas**, and they're laughing.

**Day 1 collected approximately ₹15 crore net**, with Thursday previews adding another ₹4 crore to put the total opening at a commanding **₹19 crore net**. That's the **third-highest Bollywood opening of 2026** — behind only the behemoths *Dhurandhar 2* and *Border 2* — and Akshay's second-biggest comedy opening in the post-COVID era.

But here's what's making the trade sit up. Saturday didn't just hold — it **jumped**. By evening, Day 2 had already crossed ₹18 crore net with night shows still filling up, tracking toward a ₹20 crore finish. That's a clean 35% growth over Day 1. BookMyShow ticket sales surged 35% compared to Friday. Evening-show occupancy hit 49% in NCR, 48% in Mumbai, and a scorching 55% in Lucknow.

The two-day domestic total stands at approximately **₹36 crore net** and rising. Opening weekend projections have climbed to **₹55 crore or higher**.

> "He works with a great sense of responsibility and dedication," co-star Akshara Singh revealed, noting that Akshay shot the now-viral 'Ghis Ghis Ghis' song number while running a 104-degree fever. — Bollywood Hungama

Let's talk about the elephant — or elephants — in the room: the cast. Director **Ahmed Khan** didn't just assemble an ensemble; he built an army. **Suniel Shetty** and **Arshad Warsi** return from the original, flanked by **Raveena Tandon**, **Lara Dutta**, **Jacqueline Fernandez**, **Disha Patani**, **Paresh Rawal**, **Johnny Lever**, **Rajpal Yadav**, **Tusshar Kapoor**, and **Shreyas Talpade**. That's 34 actors across 2 hours and 45 minutes of cheerful chaos. Every scene feels like the greenroom at a Filmfare party.

The audience verdict? Warm, satisfying, exactly what was promised. Not the kind of film that rewrites cinematic grammar — but the kind that gets your uncle to actually put his phone away. After a first half of 2026 dominated by brooding thrillers and intense actioners, *Welcome To The Jungle* offers something almost radical in its simplicity: an invitation to stop thinking and start cackling.

**For the diaspora, the franchise has always been a family-reunion staple.** The original *Welcome* (2007) and *Welcome Back* (2015) are still on rotation in living rooms from Edison to Southall. This instalment is tracking strong overseas, with approximately **₹4.75 crore gross on Day 1** and the opening weekend projected at **₹17 crore gross** internationally.

In the broader context of 2026's stacked release calendar — which has already produced ₹1,400 crore worth of box office business in June alone — *Welcome To The Jungle* has carved out a clean lane. It's not competing for the same audience as **Alpha** (which arrives July 3 with **Alia Bhatt** in full spy-mode) or **Dhamaal 4** (July 10). It's competing for the same audience as dinner-and-a-movie — and winning.

**Akshay Kumar now has two films in the year's Top 5 openers**, with *Bhooth Bangla* (which opened at ₹18 crore and ran to nearly ₹293 crore worldwide) sitting right behind. If *Welcome To The Jungle* follows a similar trajectory — and the Saturday surge strongly suggests it could — the lifetime total could chase **₹150 crore net domestically**.

The bottom line? Ten thousand shows on Day 2. Families streaming in for afternoon screenings. Evening shows above 30% occupancy across every major metro. This is the kind of weekend Bollywood hasn't seen from a comedy in years — and the night shows haven't even reported yet.

Grab the family. Skip the subtitles. Surrender to the madness.
